International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health (ICF) Inter-related (WHO, 2002)

International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health (ICF) • provides a standard language for classifying • body functions and structures, activities, participation levels & conditions in the world around us that influence health • classify health & health related - domains- assess health, functioning, activities & environmentalfactors • framework of the World Health • Organization (WHO) for measuring health and disability at both individuals and population levels

Dimensions of ICF Health Conditions Disease: a known or identifiable cause, such as a virus, bacteria, genetic mutation, or other biological malfunction Contextual Factors Personal factors: gender, age, coping styles, social background, education, experience, characters… Environmental factors: external physical / social factors (e.g. stairs, slopes, caregiver, employer, etc. •

Dimensions of ICF Body functions: physiological functions Activities: is the execution of a task or of body systems, including psychological action by an individual (e.g. self care, functions (e.g. sensory functions, mobility, communication) speech functions) Participation: involvement in a life Body structures: anatomical parts of the situation (e.g. employment, go to body, such as organ & limbs (e.g. eye, church, social gathering) ear, nerve, bones, muscles)

Short-term goals corresponds to body function & structure in ICF (impairment level) able to improve / manage in relatively shorter period e.g. decrease pain at low back e.g. decrease swelling at right knee e.g. improve active range of motion at left shoulder

Long-term goals corresponds to activity / participation in ICF (functional level) need relatively longer period to achieve E.g. independence in dressing/ bathing E.g. able to walk with stick independently
